findings.title: Invalidate existing local recovery codes when replacing them in user storage
findings.body: When the external storage accepts the new codes, this method leaves any existing locally stored recovery-code credential untouched. This affects users enrolled before this change, when recovery codes were always created locally. Credential validation can fall back to the local provider when external validation fails, so their old recovery codes remain usable after regeneration. Remove the previous local recovery-code credential when successfully replacing it externally, and test that codes from the previous set are rejected.

findings.title: Exercise consumption and exhaustion of federated recovery codes
findings.body: The new recovery-code validator only checks membership and never consumes the accepted code. In addition, getCredentials reconstructs a fresh credential from the entire original list each time. Consequently, this fixture allows unlimited reuse, always presents the first code, and never exercises the authenticator's exhausted-code handling. The new integration test stops after one login and therefore passes despite these broken lifecycle semantics. Make the fixture persist consumption state and extend the test to verify replay rejection, advancement to the next code, and regeneration after exhaustion.
